boundary: R-452 proves only an abstract implication: if an owner-supplied total two-orientation history error obeys a common one-step recurrence with kappa<1 and the R-451 geometric source envelope, then its exact resolvent bound vanishes. It does not supply kappa, the recurrence, a common domain, an exhaustion map, or any physical or continuum identification.
decision_reason: This is the next non-duplicative T-054 analytic interface after R-451. It reduces the missing owner-level all-history transfer to a falsifiable one-step recurrence and a strict kappa<1 threshold, while retaining the exact R-451 source envelope and all existing method and promotion boundaries.
decision_scope: T0 claim-nonbearing conditional recurrence-resolvent algebra. The result is a reusable admission contract only; it introduces no actual Q3 history, source owner, common domain, finite grid, physical selection, continuum limit, or tier change.
evidence_level: T0 exact conditional scalar history-resolvent recurrence envelope
finding: The exact recurrence kernel S_R(kappa,r)=sum_{j=0}^{R-1} kappa^(R-1-j) r^j obeys the one-step resolvent identity. With r=(23/26)^4 and A=16*C4_edge*78^4 inherited from R-451/R-450, H_R<=A*S_R follows for any common recurrence H_R<=kappa H_(R-1)+A r^(R-1). The nonresonant quotient and resonant branch are both exact. The sufficient threshold is 0<=kappa<1; kappa=1 and kappa>1 are rejected controls. The owner recurrence, kappa, common domain and production exhaustion map remain missing.
method: Load the hash-pinned R-451 geometric envelope and R-450 C4_edge parent run; derive r=q^4 and A from those parent values without fitting.
Define the total two-orientation fourth-power history error H_R and the one-step owner contract H_R<=kappa H_(R-1)+A r^(R-1), with H_0=0.
Recompute the finite resolvent sum, both closed-form branches, and the strict kappa<1 threshold using exact Fractions over the declared radius and control cases.
Run an independent non-importing reconstruction, hostile threshold/lineage/method mutations, the integrated verifier and Lean R452 arithmetic.
Keep the actual Q3 history, source-owned kappa, common domain, exhaustion, common-alpha, physical and continuum fields explicitly open.
missing_assumptions: A source-owned Q3LOCK derivation of the one-step recurrence and a value or bound kappa<1.
A common unbounded operator/form domain in which the recurrence error is defined and propagated.
Source-, beta-, cutoff-, volume-, shape-, phase- and history-uniform recurrence constants.
A proved production all-shape exhaustion map and identification of the same observable across shapes.
OS/KMS/GNS identification, common alpha, sector coercivity, physical-empty comparison, continuum, Yang--Mills and mass-gap conclusions.
next_action: When a source-owned Q3 history supplies a uniform one-step recurrence, instantiate its kappa and source residual in R-452 and feed the resulting vanishing envelope to R-451. Until then, continue the existing T-054 owner-intake boundary and the additive T-059/T-061 observation-source lock without another finite table.
no_overclaim: R-452 is a conditional scalar resolvent interface, not an actual Q3LOCK history, operator-domain theorem, common-alpha result, physical-sector result, continuum result or Yang--Mills/mass-gap proof.
question: Can the direct R-451 history-tail input be replaced by a scalar one-step state-weighted recurrence, and what exact resolvent envelope and threshold follows without a finite-table extrapolation?
stop_or_redesign: If the owner recurrence has kappa>=1, retain only the exact threshold diagnostic and record the local failure; do not relax the threshold after target disclosure.
If the recurrence residual is not bounded by the parent R-451 source envelope, keep the resolvent identity but record the source-term mismatch.
If kappa or the recurrence depends on shape, volume, cutoff, beta or history depth, do not call it a uniform Q3 estimate.
If no common domain is supplied, do not convert the scalar envelope into an operator or form theorem.
If a proposed use changes the established method or owner order, return to the continuity gate before proceeding.
